items.content: The last light came slowly, the way light always does when it means to linger. It settled on the highest edges of buildings like something reverent, gilding the water towers and cornices in a pale amber that had no business being so beautiful above a city so indifferent. Down in the streets, the shadows had already thickened into evening, but up there the day still held on, reluctant, burning quietly against the blue.

items.content: She had not expected it. Drawing back the curtain, she found the world remade — the garden gone white and quiet beneath a sky the colour of old pewter, every familiar edge softened into something almost unrecognisable. The oak tree held its snow like a secret it had been keeping through the dark hours. She stood there in her socks on the cold floorboards, coffee cooling in her hand, reluctant to look away.

items.content: She found it tucked between the pages of a novel she had always meant to finish, the envelope still sealed, her mother's handwriting looping across the front in that familiar, urgent slant. The letter was addressed to no one — or perhaps to everyone — and for a long moment she simply held it, feeling the weight of words that had never broken free into the world. Whatever was inside had lived its whole life in darkness, patient as a seed that never found soil. She set it on the table and made herself a cup of tea, not yet ready to be the one who finally let it breathe.
